harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: On node1, configured /etc/cron.allow to restrict crontab scheduling to only root and opsadmin (created the opsadmin user, which did not previously exist). Verified enforcement by testing an allowed user and a denied user before and after a full node restart, confirming the restriction and cron service persist across reboot via a changed boot_id.
actions_performed: Inspected baseline OS/cron state on node1 (Ubuntu 16.04, cron 3.0pl1)
Created opsadmin user (did not previously exist)
Created and later removed a throwaway 'cronprobe' user to prove denial
Wrote /etc/cron.allow containing only 'root' and 'opsadmin', removed any /etc/cron.deny
Verified root and opsadmin can create crontabs; verified cronprobe is denied with 'cannot use this program (crontab)'
Cleaned up test crontab entries and the cronprobe user
Captured baseline boot_id and cron.service health before restart
Issued a native reboot (shutdown -r now) on node1, acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec was available again
Confirmed boot_id changed (b185f188... -> a9825e77...), proving an actual restart occurred
Post-restart: verified cron.service active, /etc/cron.allow persisted with root/opsadmin only, opsadmin user persisted, opsadmin can schedule cron jobs, and user 'nobody' is denied

evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs (baseline enforcement)
evidence.summary: Inspected initial state (no cron.allow/deny, opsadmin missing), then created opsadmin, wrote /etc/cron.allow with root+opsadmin, and proved root/opsadmin crontab writes succeed while a throwaway user 'cronprobe' is denied with 'cannot use this program (crontab)'.
Captured boot_id b185f188-42be-40d1-84ea-f7c9a76f5c8d, cron.service active/running, and /etc/cron.allow contents prior to restart.

evidence.requirement: Node restart acknowledgement returns before disconnect
evidence.summary: Issued 'shutdown -r now' via a backgrounded sudo command; the ack printed before the SSH connection was dropped by the reboot.

evidence.requirement: Node restart is unavailable then recovers
evidence.summary: First poll after reboot got 'Connection refused' (node down); next poll succeeded once cron was back up.

evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity (real restart, not just service restart)
evidence.summary: boot_id changed from b185f188-42be-40d1-84ea-f7c9a76f5c8d (pre-restart) to a9825e77-e143-4ec0-aa52-61a323eebd18 (post-restart).

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of cron access control and service
evidence.summary: After restart, cron.service is active, /etc/cron.allow still lists only root/opsadmin, opsadmin user persisted, opsadmin can schedule a cron job successfully, and user 'nobody' is denied crontab access.

attempts.summary: On node1, configured /etc/cron.allow to restrict crontab scheduling to only root and opsadmin (created the opsadmin user, which did not previously exist). Verified enforcement by testing an allowed user and a denied user before and after a full node restart, confirming the restriction and cron service persist across reboot via a changed boot_id.
